name: ransomware_family_match
description: Give candidate ransomware families and variants for what an examination observed, from a small reviewed reference set, and say how far each candidate is supported. The tool is the correlation layer; the `yara` program is the engine for note text. It reads the sealed values file of `ransom_note_scan` by reference (`values_file`: ransom-note-values.jsonl; the tool therefore declares secret_output `required`): from it only the note id and the last component of the path of each note row (kind note_preview) are taken, to match note names and to hand the note files to yara; no indicator, identifier, preview, value or path is printed. It also takes the extensions the caller observed (`extensions`, at most 100000 strings of at most 300 characters) and further note names (`note_names`), and optionally a date (`observed_on`). REFERENCE SET: reference/entries.json (project-authored, AGPL-3.0-or-later, seven families, each entry with `reviewed_on`, `fresh_until`, an `evidence_strength`, variants with `valid_for`, features and the numbered sources it cites: a URL, the page's own dates and the date it was read) and reference/rules.yar (two text rules, each with a `rule_version`); reference/reference-manifest.json holds the sha256 of both. The sha256 are checked at every run and a mismatch, a missing file or a file the manifest does not list is a refusal (status failed, `reference_set_used` false): the job service checks only the sha256 of run.py, so the tool checks its own data. A manifest and files changed together are caught by the pack seal, not by this check. The set is a SNAPSHOT of what the cited pages said on the date shown, not a catalogue: no match does not mean that an unknown family is absent, a family that is not in the set cannot be named, and a name or an extension can be shared by families or reused by a later build. The set has a freshness date (`reference_set.fresh_until`); an entry past `fresh_until` is reported as stale on its candidate row, and a matched stale entry, or a set past its date, makes the answer partial. FEATURES: an extension (an exact extension or a pattern, case-folded), a note name (exact or a pattern, case-folded, the last path component) and a note text rule (yara). Each feature has a strength: strong (two or more publishers in the cited sources), moderate (one publisher) or weak (a shape only, or a generic name that other families also use, such as readme.txt). A candidate is `corroborated` when two kinds of feature that are neither generic nor shape-only matched, `single_feature` when one kind did with at least moderate strength, and `weak_lead` otherwise. A shape-only extension (BlackCat's seven characters) counts when a matched note name embeds the same characters; when the note embeds other characters the extension is dropped and the answer lists a `note_name_embeds_another_extension` contradiction. THE OUTCOME is one word: `unidentified` (nothing supports a candidate), `candidate` (one family), `leading_candidate` (several families, one strictly better supported; the others are listed, not excluded) or `ambiguous` (two or more families supported alike; `tied_families` names them, and `variant_ambiguity` names variants of one family supported alike). `contradictions` lists features of different kinds that support disjoint variants (for example an extension of one family and a note name of another). `period_check` compares `observed_on` with the dates of the sources cited for a candidate's matched features (`within_cited_sources`, `before_cited_sources`, `after_cited_sources`, `not_stated`): it is a note about the snapshot, not a contradiction. A family match NEVER names an affiliate or an actor: the reference set has no such field and the answer says so. The tool fetches nothing and runs nothing but yara. WHAT IS PRINTED: the family and variant ids, the reference feature ids, the strength, the source ids with their title, publisher and dates, the yara rule id and version, the byte offsets of a text rule's hit in a note (the candidate rows show at most 3 offsets of 5 notes per rule; the table `note_text_hits` holds every hit with all its offsets, at most 100000 per note, and the candidates table is written whole when it is longer than `limit`), the note ids of ransom_note_scan, the position of an observed extension in the caller's own list, and counts. No observed extension, note name, path, indicator or note text is printed anywhere (a canary placed in a note, a name or an extension is not in the answer or in any file the tool writes); matched text that yara prints is parsed for the offset and dropped. The filter (`filter`) restricts which reference entries are considered, by their shown text (id, name, variant id and label), before matching: counts and the outcome are of that scope, and no filter, sort or count follows a hidden value. YARA: with `yara` absent the extension and name matching still run, the text rules do not, and the answer is partial and says so. At most `max_notes` (default 2000) note files are given to yara, in batches of 100, each at most `max_note_bytes` (default 1 MiB, at most 16 MiB); the rest are matched by name and counted in the reasons. Each note is opened without following a link and only a regular file is listed for yara, which writes nothing. `status` (also `complete`) is `complete` only when the reference set matched its manifest and is fresh, every row of the values file was read, every note file was given to yara and nothing was cut by a bound or by the clock; otherwise it is `partial` with `status_basis` and `partial_reasons`. The tool's own clock `max_seconds` (default 240, at most 270, below the manifest's 300) is checked before every batch and every row; yara is ended with what it started when the clock runs out. Tables longer than `limit` are written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends yara and what it started, then ends the tool with one JSON answer (status failed, interrupted, exit code 128 + the signal) after removing the pages it was writing. The handlers are installed when the tool's module code has run as far as its stop block: the start of the interpreter and the compiling of the file come first, and a stop signal in that window can end the tool with no JSON answer at all. SIGKILL cannot be caught: a tool killed that way leaves the hidden temporary files of the pages in tool-output and, in a window of microseconds, an empty file at a result name; delete them. The job's own timeout_seconds (300) is not passed to the tool: give max_seconds a value below it, because a job stopped by its timeout answers failed, not partial. A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential, a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape. Residuals, listed and not fixed: the number of notes, of distinct note names and of observed extensions are printed (derived counts); a note larger than `max_note_bytes` is not matched by text; a note replaced between that check and yara's own read is not guarded against; and a ransom note that is an image or a PDF is matched by text only if its bytes hold the phrase of a rule. yara's hits are read from a pipe while it runs and, after it has ended, for at most one second and 1 MiB: a process it left holding the pipe is ended by the shared process block before the pipe is closed and the pipe is let go (a cut at 1 MiB is said in `partial_reasons`), a yara that exited is not reported as timed out, and the answer is `partial` (a line in `partial_reasons`) because what that process would still have printed is not in the hits. A call that ran yara carries `program_group` (`subreaper`, `left_behind`, `unproven`, `notes`) in its answer; one that did not carries none. The tool reads only what yara printed, so a host that cannot adopt orphans (not Linux, or the kernel refuses PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) does not make the answer `partial`: `program_group.unproven` says it.

values_file.description: The sealed values file of ransom_note_scan (ransom-note-values.jsonl), read by reference in a secret_output job. Only the note id and the last path component of each note_preview row are used

extensions.description: Extensions observed on encrypted files (at most 100000 strings of at most 300 characters each; a leading dot is added when missing). A compound suffix such as .id[...].[...].ext is matched whole

note_names.description: Further note file names observed (the last path component is taken), matched like the names from the values file

observed_on.description: A date, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM, compared with the dates of the sources of each candidate (period_check)

as_of.description: The date freshness is judged on, YYYY-MM-DD (default: today, UTC)

filter.description: Only reference entries whose shown text (id, name, variant id or label) contains this text are considered; counts and the outcome are of that scope

limit.description: Rows shown inline in the candidates table (default 50); every row is counted, and a table with more is written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages.candidates.all_results

max_notes.description: The most note files given to yara (default 2000, at most 100000); the rest are matched by name only and counted in partial_reasons

max_note_bytes.description: The largest note file given to yara (default 1048576, at least 16, at most 16777216); a larger one is not matched by text and is counted

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 240, at most 270; the manifest's timeout is 300). When it runs out no further batch is given to yara, what was matched is reported, and the answer is partial
